subject: Recap & runbook: HealthLytics reserved GPU island — constraints, burst plan, SLO targets
messages:
From: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@healthlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync — inference capacity needs

Thanks for the call today — good to get aligned. Summary from our side: we run GenAI-assisted chart summarization for clinicians (HIPAA scope) and are seeing inconsistent latency and noisy tail behavior during spikes. Our main asks were: a) full isolation for PHI workloads, b) predictable p95/p99 latency for 256-512 token flows, c) ability to burst for processing nightly ingestion windows without multi-day procurement cycles.

Two clarifying items:
- We need KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and audit logs for model calls.
- Preferred hosting region is us-west2 (GCP).

Next steps we suggested: sizing workbook from you, a security checklist for our compliance team, and a pilot reserved island to validate p99 under production-like traffic. Happy to aim for a procurement decision by end of Q1.

—Tom
Tom Weaver
VP Engineering, HealthLytics
~ops@healthlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync — inference capacity needs

Tom — thanks, captured everything clearly. Below is a short post-call runbook and the immediate asks we can take on this week.

Runbook (high level):
- Pain points confirmed: multi-tenant interference causing latency tail, procurement friction for burst ops, and compliance/KMS requirements.
- Goal: offer a 90-day pilot of a Reserved GPU island (single-tenant pool) in us-west2 to validate p99 targets and operational runbook before a longer reserved commit.
- SLO targets we discussed: baseline target p95 < 180ms, p99 < 320ms for 512-token inference; sustained throughput target ~150 concurrent rps equivalent (we'll model this in the workbook).
- Isolation: single-tenant pool + encrypted-at-rest with KMS (customer key). We will provide audit logs and request tracing to meet your compliance reviewer needs.
- Burst model: base committed pool sized for steady-state; automated burst nodes for nightly ingestion windows with a configurable max burst budget and automatic fallback to lower-cost compatible model variants if capacity saturated.

Immediate deliverables (by Fri):
1) Compute workbook populated with our initial sizing assumptions and an editable sheet for your traffic profiles (attachment: HealthLytics-compute-workbook.xlsx).
2) Draft SLA + ops runbook tailored to pilot (attachment: redwood-dedicated-sla-template.pdf).
3) Security checklist for your compliance team + KMS onboarding steps (I'll loop Security if you want deeper review).

Proposed next meeting: technical deep dive + security Q&A — Thu Dec 3 at 10:00am PT. If that works, we'll ask our infra engineer (Ben) to share expected token-level cost ranges and batching recommendations during the call.

Questions for you now:
- Can you share a 24-hour representative traffic sample (CSV) to drop into the workbook?
- Is PHI present in the request body or only metadata (helps map audit scope)?

Thanks — I'll attach the workbook now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Laura King <laura.king@healthlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@healthlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync — inference capacity needs

Marissa — thanks for the clear runbook. A couple of notes from procurement & security:

- Procurement timeline: target internal PO/contract decision by 2027-03-28, but we can run the pilot earlier if legal review for the SLA template is light.
- Security asks: we will need a SOC2 extract and details on data retention windows for request logs; KMS with rotation policy must be supported. Can you confirm if Redwood supports HSM-backed KMS (customer-managed) or if we need an extra integration step?
- Billing preference: monthly invoice for the pilot, with a credit for early termination if the pilot isn't extended.

We'll drop a 24-hour traffic sample into the workbook (expect that later today). The PHI is present in request bodies (redacted fields) — we will provide a template of redaction rules for the compliance team.

Looking forward to Thu's deep dive.

Laura King
Director, Procurement & Security, HealthLytics
laura.king@healthlytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@healthlytics.com>, Laura King <laura.king@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick sync — inference capacity needs

Hi Tom / Laura — quick technical notes ahead of Thu's call: 

- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (HSM-backed via supported cloud KMS providers). We'll include the KMS onboarding checklist in the security packet.
- Bursting behavior: our Dedicated runtime can cold-start extra nodes in ~2–5 minutes depending on model size; we'll size burst budgets conservatively in the workbook and model warm-cache impact. For critical low-latency windows we recommend enabling a small warm standby to keep KV caches primed.
- Sizing note: to hit the p99 target at 512 tokens we recommend the pilot pool start at 8x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) with autoscale headroom up to +4 GPUs for bursts — we'll show cost delta in the workbook.
- Billing: monthly invoicing for pilot is fine; Marissa will draft the termination credit language with Sales Ops.

Marissa — attached a one-page ops brief (burst-policy-proposal.md) and I've added a short tab in the workbook with our starting GPU recommendations. See you Thu 10:00am PT.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199
